title: Interleaved stream + toolcall fidelity: schema-fingerprint regression harness
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Summary:
Build a deterministic, CI-friendly regression harness that validates the interaction surface between streaming responses, interleaved tool/function calls, and structured output schemas. The harness will create compact "fingerprints" of expected structured payloads generated from a curated set of golden prompts and assert compatibility across runtime changes (kernel selection, batching, kv-cache priming, and response-sharding). This ticket covers design, implementation, CI integration, and a short rollout plan.

Background and rationale:
- Recent runtime changes (batch scheduler + kernel fallbacks) introduced subtle interleavings where toolcall markers and structured JSON fragments can be emitted across frames. Upstream teams rely on stable contract behavior.
- Existing suites validate streaming and structured output separately; we need a focused cross-cutting suite that: 1) reproduces interleaving patterns seen in production, 2) conservatively fingerprints structured payloads and toolcall metadata, and 3) runs fast enough for CI gating.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can reproduce at least 12 representative interleaving scenarios (short/long prefixes, mid-stream toolcall, nested toolcall + function-return, kv-cache-primed continuations).
- For each scenario, harness computes a schema-fingerprint (canonical key ordering + normalized numeric/string canonicalization) and compares against stored golden fingerprints.
- CI job runs the smoke subset (4 fast cases) on every merge; a full run is scheduled nightly and on release branches.
- Failures produce a machine-readable JSON report with diff hints and a reproducible seed and traffic trace URL.
- Documentation for adding new golden prompts and regenerating fingerprints exists in the repo README.

High-level plan:
1) Design canonicalization and fingerprint format (SHA256 of canonical NDJSON lines after normalization).
2) Implement interleaving emulator that can inject delay and sequence-splitting to simulate partial frames and network batching.
3) Harvest a corpus of golden prompts from product teams + create synthetic edge cases.
4) Implement validators: schema-aware comparator (allow small numeric jitter), toolcall-idempotency checks, and prefix-tolerant matching for partial frames.
5) Wire harness into CI with two jobs: quick-smoke (parallel, containerized) and nightly-full.
6) Add dashboards for history of fingerprint diffs and flaky-case triage.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Fingerprint vs full-text diff: fingerprint is compact and fast for CI, but we store expanded artifacts (trace + canonicalized output) when failures occur to enable debugging.
- Strictness: Default comparator is tolerant to whitespace and insignificant numeric jitter; teams can opt-in to strict comparisons when rolling out breaking changes.
- Emulation fidelity: We prioritize scenarios seen in production over exhaustive fuzzing; fuzz harness will be a follow-up ticket.

Acceptance tests / QA steps:
- Run quick-smoke locally using Dockerized harness with seed=42 and verify fingerprints match stored golden for linux-amd64.
- Create a staged PR that intentionally changes kernel scheduling to trigger a known fingerprint regression; ensure CI fails with a useful diff report.
- Validate that nightly run posts artifacts to the regression S3 bucket and a Grafana metric increments on diffs.

Rollback / mitigation plan for flakey CI failures:
- Quarantine flaky case by moving it to nightly-only and open ENG follow-up for root cause.
- Provide an opt-out label on PRs to bypass smoke gate while hotfixes are deployed (requires senior eng approval).
